name: Defereggental
kurzbeschreibung: The Defereggental in East Tyrol: a pristine high-alpine valley in the Hohe Tauern National Park with the Jagdhausalm founded in 1212, stone pine forests, and healing thermal water.
preis: Tal und Passstraße mautfrei (Mautstraße Erlsbach–Oberhaus ca. 9,00 €)
oeffnungszeiten: Tal ganzjährig frei zugänglich; Stallersattel Ende Mai bis Ende Oktober
beschreibung:
Overview

The picturesque Defereggental in the heart of East Tyrol is one of the most pristine, least developed high-alpine valleys in the entire Eastern Alps. Framed by over 50 three-thousand-meter peaks of the Rieserfernergruppe, the Venedigergruppe, and the Deferegger Alpen, the valley extends for 35 kilometres along the rushing Schwarzach river up to the 2,052-metre-high Stallersattel on the border with South Tyrol. Large parts of the valley belong to the Nationalpark Hohe Tauern. With its three traditional mountain municipalities of Hopfgarten, St. Veit (at 1,495 m, the highest municipality in East Tyrol), and the main village of St. Jakob, the Defereggental delights recreation seekers and nature lovers with living traditions and alpine tranquility.

Nature & Cultural Highlights

Settlement of this high valley dates back millennia: prehistoric resting sites at Hirschbühel prove that Stone Age hunters roamed the valley as early as 7,000 BC. The most famous cultural monument of the inner valley is the Jagdhausalm, situated at 2,009 metres above sea level: first documented in 1212, it is considered the oldest documented alpine pasture village in all of Austria. With its 16 protected natural stone huts and the Maria-Hilf-Kapelle, the ensemble is reminiscent of a Tibetan mountain settlement and is affectionately known as the „Klein-Tibet der Alpen“. St. Jakob is also home to a unique geological phenomenon: in 2004, deep drilling at 1,850 metres discovered Deferegger Heilwasser – a 600,000-year-old, highly mineralized sodium chloride iodine thermal brine from prehistoric seawater that provides relief for skin and respiratory ailments. In addition, the valley boasts the Oberhauser Zirbenwald (approx. 800 hectares), the largest contiguous stone pine forest in the entire Eastern Alps.

Visit & Getting There

The valley and its hiking areas are freely accessible throughout the year. The pass road over the Stallersattel (2,052 m) to South Tyrol is open from late May to late October (closed at night from 22:15 to 05:30; traffic-light-controlled one-way system on the South Tyrolean side). The toll road from Erlsbach to Gasthof Oberhaus is open in summer (approx. €9.00 per car); from there, visitors continue on foot or via alpine taxi to the Jagdhausalm. Getting there by public transport: take the train to Lienz station, then take the VVT bus line 953 directly into the Defereggental to St. Jakob; in summer, the Deferegger Wanderbus connects the alpine pastures and the Stallersattel. By car: from the north via Mittersill and the Felbertauernstraße B108 to Huben, turning off onto the L25 Defereggentalstraße.

Tips

The Deferegger Heilwasserwelt in St. Jakob with its myth square and Kneipp fountain is fully wheelchair accessible; the lakeshore trail around idyllic Obersee at the Stallersattel pass summit is also ideal for seniors and pushchairs. For the path to the Jagdhausalm (approx. 7 km gravel road from Oberhaus), an all-terrain e-mountain bike or the convenient alpine taxi is recommended. Stop by the rustic alpine huts and sample authentic East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen.
